title: Eval scenario
description: One scenario: the conversation, the world the agent sees, and the properties its execution trace must have. Scenarios are DATA, not code (AI-EVALS.md §3). This schema is deliberately strict — `additionalProperties: false` everywhere — because a mistyped assertion key must fail validation loudly rather than be silently ignored, which would turn the scenario into a test that checks nothing while reporting green.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. `amb-002-next-friday-on-a-friday`. The prefix is the class. IDs are never reused or renumbered: a baseline diff is meaningless if an id can change meaning.

class.description: The five classes every agent suite carries (AI-EVALS.md §3). A suite with no adversarial class is testing the demo, not the product.

title.description: One line, human-readable, stating the situation rather than the mechanism.

why.description: What this scenario would catch if it broke. A scenario that cannot answer this is decoration, and decoration is what makes a suite slow without making it safer.

origin.description: Where the scenario came from. Scenarios extracted from a real failure are worth more than invented ones, and §3 requires every production incident to become a scenario before it becomes a fix — so the provenance is tracked rather than remembered.

reference.description: Issue, trace id, or incident reference. No customer names, no personal data.

gate.description: constraint = must pass at 100%, hard-blocks the merge. behaviour = measured against the recorded baseline. A scenario asserting a hard constraint from docs/SPEC.md §3 MUST be `constraint`; the schema cannot enforce that, so it is a review item.

fixture.description: The world the agent sees. Everything is pinned: there is no ambient clock, no ambient timezone, and no data that is not written down here or in the named base fixture. `clock` and `timezone` are required, not optional — a scenario that passes only in August is not a scenario.

base.description: Name of a file in evals/fixtures/, without extension. Shared seed data lives there so 30 scenarios do not carry 30 copies of the same employee list.

clock.description: The instant the agent believes it is, with offset. Injected, never read from the host — a scenario whose result depends on the day it runs is not a scenario.

timezone.description: IANA zone for the acting user. Date resolution happens here, not in UTC.

overrides.description: Sparse changes on top of the base fixture: permissions removed, a leave type renamed, an extra colliding leave. Only the delta is written, so the interesting part of a scenario is the part that differs.

tool_behaviour.description: Fault injection per tool, for the degradation class. Absent means every tool succeeds.

outcome.description: http_403 is distinct from a permission fixture: the former is the backend refusing at call time, the latter is the agent never being entitled to call.

after_calls.description: Succeed this many times first, then fail. Models the tool that dies mid-conversation.

conversation.description: User turns, and the confirmation replies that resolve a gate. The agent's turns are NOT scripted here — they are what is under test.

role.description: `confirmation` is a separate role on purpose. A confirmation is not chat: it is a decision on a specific drafted request, consumed by the agent as a `confirmation.received` event. Modelling it as a user message would let a plausible-sounding sentence stand in for an explicit approval.

expect.description: Assertions over the TRACE, not over the reply text (AI-EVALS.md §4). At least one is required: a scenario with no assertion is the guard-then-bail failure in its purest form.

rubrics.description: Layer-2 criteria that apply. Empty or absent means Layer 1 alone grades this scenario, which is correct for most constraint scenarios.

skip.description: An unimplemented scenario is `skip` WITH A REASON, never a silent pass and never a deleted file (AI-EVALS.md §4). The harness reports skips distinctly from passes, and a skip count above zero is visible in every run.

toolName.description: The internal IWorkforceTools surface — normalised at the anti-corruption boundary (P11). Scenarios never name a vendor's tool; if the external dialect changes, no scenario changes.

not.description: Both together is a silent no-op: the evaluator reads `times` and ignores `at_least`, so an author who wrote both would believe a bound the harness never checked. F-1 was exactly this shape of slack.

oneOf.description: Absence. Half of the two-assertion rule for a denied path: assert the refusal AND that the call never happened.
Ordering. `no write before a confirmation event` is expressed here rather than in prose.

not.description: Both together is a silent no-op: the evaluator reads `times` and ignores `at_least`.

oneOf.description: The agent's decision is a trace attribute, not a phrase in its reply. Layer 1 must never grade prose (see docs/adr/0003).
Termination by decision, never by hitting the iteration cap (AI-EVALS.md §4).

Grounding as a STRUCTURAL property: the argument value must appear in an earlier tool result in the same trace. This is what stops a hallucinated leave-type id being graded as 'fluent and confident' by a judge.
No internal identifier appears in user-facing output. Fixture ids are synthetic and greppable by construction, so this is decidable rather than heuristic.

Escape hatch for a span attribute with no dedicated assertion. Deliberately last and deliberately verbose: reaching for it often means the vocabulary above is missing a concept, which is a finding about the schema, not about the agent.
